title: pdeq.json
description: Configuration file for a PDEQ install. Controls path resolution for specs, code, and nested/monorepo setups.

pdeqVersion.description: Pdeq version that this project's specs and config conform to. Set by scripts/init.sh on install and updated by /pdeq-migrate. A missing value means the project predates the migrations feature.

specsRoot.description: Relative path from this config file to the directory containing product/, design/, engineering/, qa/, and roadmap/ folders. Defaults to '.' (same directory as pdeq.json).

codeRoot.description: Relative path from this config file to the source code root. Used by the bootstrap analyzer. May point outside the pdeq directory.

platforms.description: List of platform IDs supported by this project. Supplements or replaces the platform table in CLAUDE.md. Each ID corresponds to a subfolder in design/, engineering/, and qa/.

harnesses.description: Coding-agent harnesses this project supports. Drives per-harness file materialization in scripts/init.sh: each enabled harness gets its expected agent-instructions file (CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, etc.) at each lane and, when applicable, a slash-command directory. Omit to default to ['claude'] for v0.3.x back-compat. Realizes FR-harness-agnostic-config and FR-harness-agnostic-v1-harness-set.

pdeqDir.description: Path to the .pdeq submodule or framework directory, relative to the git root. Defaults to '.pdeq'.

selfHost.description: True when this config belongs to the pdeq repository itself (framework files live at the repo root rather than under .pdeq/). Controls whether the traceability audit scans into framework directories. Consumer projects leave this false.

codeMappingExclude.description: Additional glob patterns (relative to the git root) excluded from the traceability audit's marker scan. Appended to the default exclusion list (node_modules, vendor, dist, build, etc.).

laneAudit.description: Project-specific red-flag terms for the lane-discipline lexical backstop (scripts/audit-lanes.sh). Each array EXTENDS (never replaces) the built-in default term list, so configuring a project's own vocabulary adds to the shipped guard rather than silencing it. Terms are matched as literal, word-boundary alternatives against product specs. The category split is for self-documentation and mirrors the agent lane-review taxonomy; the deterministic audit greps the union of all four. Omit entirely to use only the built-in defaults. Realizes FR-lane-discipline-project-terms.

vendors.description: Vendor / service names that must not appear in platform-neutral product specs.

protocols.description: Protocol or algorithm names (auth flows, wire protocols, crypto primitives) that indicate engineering bleed.

platforms.description: Host or platform names that should not be treated as the product itself in a shared product spec.

libraries.description: Library or framework names that are engineering decisions, not product requirements.

exclude.description: Default red-flag terms this project has judged domain-legitimate (a platform it must run on, a language it supports, a first-class domain noun). The deterministic checks — both the warn-only backstop and the blocking structural/downstream checks — strip these terms before matching, so they neither warn nor block. Stripping is surgical: a non-excluded flagged term on the same line still flags. Does not affect the advisory lane review. Realizes FR-lane-discipline-exclude-terms.

temporalAudit.description: Configuration for the temporal language audit (scripts/audit-temporal.sh), which detects phasing/versioning language in authoritative specs. Introduced in pdeq 0.10.0. Realizes FR-living-spec-temporal-audit-modes.

patterns.description: Custom temporal language patterns to scan for. REPLACES the default pattern list. Each pattern is a grep-compatible extended regex. Omit to use built-in defaults (MVP, 'phase N', 'V2', 'iteration N', 'will be added', etc.).

blockCommit.description: Whether the pre-commit hook blocks commits when temporal language is detected. Defaults to TRUE (pristine specs enforced). Set to false only if the project needs incremental cleanup; this opt-out is visible in version control.

nested.description: Configuration for nested installs (inside a monorepo package or feature subdirectory). Omit for root-level installs.

repoRoot.description: Relative path from this config file up to the actual git root. Used to correctly resolve symlink targets for scripts and .claude/commands.

label.description: Human-readable name for this component or module. Used in agent context messages to clarify scope. Defaults to the directory name.

examples.$comment: Root install — PDEQ and code live side-by-side at the repo root
Install with a project-tuned lane-audit term list — the deterministic backstop also flags this project's vendors/protocols/platforms/libraries
Nested install — PDEQ lives inside a feature subfolder, used from multiple harnesses
Monorepo package install — PDEQ lives at packages/api/pdeq/
